reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) demonstrates that SCCPs improve ambient and high-temperature strength and ductility in a W-based HEA, but it provides no data or discussion on radiation tolerance, defect sink efficiency, or behaviour under ion irradiation. The key premise linking coherent interfaces to radiation defect recombination is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced point defects, enhancing recombination and reducing defect accumulation.
The coherent interfaces maintain dislocation mobility, preserving ductility under irradiation.
The SCCP heat treatment protocol (800–1100 °C stepwise) produces nanoscale coherent precipitates (δ, γ″) in a W-based refractory HEA.
The baseline alloy is a supersaturated single-phase BCC matrix that can be precipitation-hardened by the treatment.
The predicted outcome (reduced void swelling, maintained strength/ductility) is measurable under fusion-relevant ion irradiation.
